question: Directive (EU) 2019/1152 on transparent and predictable working conditions was adopted in 2019. The purpose of this Directive is to improve working conditions by promoting more transparent and predictable employment. Member States were required to transpose the directive into national law by 1 August 2022 at the latest. Will Member States that have failed to meet the deadline be penalised?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (28.6.2024) Directive (EU) 2019/11521 aims at promoting more transparent and predictable employment. Member States were required to transpose the directive into national law by 1 August 2022 at the latest. On 21 September 2022, the Commission launched infringements procedures against 19 Member States for failure to notify transposition measures in due time.

Since then, 17 Member States have notified full transposition. The Commission services are currently analysing that the transposition measures transpose fully the provisions of the Directive in conformity with the Directive’s minimum standards. In June 2023, the Commission sent Reasoned Opinions to two Member States, who have not yet notified any transposing measures.

In the case these two Member States do not fulfil their obligation and do not notify the full transposition of this Directive, the Commission may refer them to the Court of Justice of the EU. In accordance with Article 260 (3), the Commission may request the Court to impose financial sanctions on the Member States concerned and may specify the amount of the lump sum and penalty payment which it considers appropriate.
